claims.text: If we elect Fabricio, he will eliminate the rights of those he does not agree with.
If we vote for Carlos, he will guarantee equal rights for all.

implicit_assumptions: Only Fabricio and Carlos are viable candidates; any other candidate would be less desirable.
The elected candidate’s character directly determines policy outcomes on rights.

Inference.supporting_quote: Obviously, we elect evil and allow Fabricio to eliminate the rights of those he does not agree with or we vote for Carlos and guarantee equal rights for all.
Inference.premise: the comment limits the choice to only two outcomes, implying a false exclusivity.
Inference.conclusion: the claim represents a false dilemma.
Inference.defective_inference: posits that only two options exist, ignoring other candidates.
Inference.strongest_nonfallacious_reading: None, the structure itself is a false dilemma.
Inference.auxiliary_observation: no other fallacieous reasoning type applies.

Evidence.conclusion: The argument restricts choices to two extremes, improperly limiting alternatives.
Evidence.defective_inference: Presenting a false dichotomy to support a stance.

arbiter.content: The comment presents only two extreme options—Fabricio as evil or Carlos as egalitarian—implicitly excluding any other candidates or nuanced alternatives; this restricted choice forms a false dilemma. The quoted span “Obviously, we elect evil and allow Fabricio… or we vote for Carlos and guarantee equal rights for all.” evidences the misleading binary framing. Therefore the comment is Fallacious.
